criteria.criterion: The apply-layer DROP is fixed: `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` used to discard any non-`add` link record outright (`action != "add": continue`); that branch + the `rebar.unlink` wiring landed in change 1276 and is independently mutation-proven.
G1/G2/G3/G5 landed and are mutation-proven. They are dormant (nothing emits a removal for them to gate) but they are correct, and they are the guards a future implementation needs.
The shipped semantics are STATED: local-wins-and-restore. A link deleted in Jira is re-added on the next pass — convergent, no local data destroyed, identical on both backends.

The live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is XFAIL with the full reason in the marker, `strict=False` so it fails LOUDLY as an xpass the moment a removal path starts working — NOT inverted and NOT deleted. Gerrit change 1303, MERGED as 29f9627128; verified on main: reason text present, strict=False, cell body unmodified.
The ecosystem evidence is recorded, with sources, so this is not re-litigated from scratch.

The refutation of the original design is recorded, with a probe — `managed_refs` cannot distinguish 'a link we never pushed' from 'a link the peer deleted'; the two states are IDENTICAL on every input the guards read. That finding stopped a second data-loss defect before it was written.

The correct design is recorded WITH A WORKING TEMPLATE — change 1296 landed exactly this pattern for parents (a per-binding record of what the peer last had, advanced only on OBSERVATION), so whoever picks this up starts from shipped, reviewed code rather than from the refuted premise. `binding_store` is already a parameter of both link differs.
`inbound_differ.py` and `apply_inbound_records.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap.
